incidents.victim: US universities, companies and critical infrastructure
incidents.industry: Multi-sector (academia, energy, defense, healthcare, IT, finance)
incidents.attacker: Iran — IRGC and Ministry of Intelligence (MOIS)
incidents.vector: Spearphishing and stolen-credential intrusions run by the Tehran-based Mabna Institute hacking-for-hire operation.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed charges against 17 Iranians and Treasury sanctioned four; the group stole 31.5TB of academic data and IP from 144 US and 178 foreign universities, and since late 2023 exfiltrated data from US energy, defense, healthcare, IT and financial firms.

incidents.victim: Android banking and cryptocurrency wallet users
incidents.vector: ToxicPanda 2.0 Android trojan abuses Accessibility Services and Wireless Debugging/ADB for privilege escalation and lock-screen credential overlays.
incidents.impact: Updated variant adds 167 remote commands and expands targeting from 16 to 349 banking, e-wallet and crypto apps, enabling full device takeover that threatens both consumer and enterprise accounts on the device.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused the legitimate TWCore updater on DoFun car head units to silently push the JarService downloader without any user interaction.
incidents.impact: First documented malware campaign purpose-built for car head units; infected units are turned into reverse proxies for a botnet linked to the BadBox operation, routing others' traffic and generating ad fraud.

incidents.victim: Elderly residents of New York and New Jersey
incidents.vector: Overseas scammers impersonated law enforcement and government officials by phone and email, directing victims to hand over cash, gold and gift cards to money mules.
incidents.impact: A Jersey City money mule was charged with helping siphon more than $7.5 million from at least nine elderly victims; he fled to Canada and was arrested awaiting extradition.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion by a Chinese state-linked group targeting telecom infrastructure for lateral movement.
incidents.impact: T-Mobile staff physically cut an internet cable to a compromised system to stop the intruders from moving deeper into its network, per newly reported details of the campaign.

incidents.vector: The ChainDrop worm uses malicious npm preinstall scripts to launch an obfuscated payload that reads GitHub Actions runner memory to steal OIDC tokens and secrets, then self-propagates.
incidents.impact: Over 400 packages including hugely popular libraries keyv and cacheable-request were infected; the worm backdoors developer tools (VS Code, Claude Code) and manages C2 via Ethereum transactions.

incidents.victim: Rust crate ecosystem (arrayref and two libraries)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a popular Rust developer's account and injected malware into three of his libraries; infrastructure overlapped with known North Korean operations.
incidents.impact: Malicious versions of three crates — including arrayref, with nearly 5 million weekly downloads — were live for 23 minutes before the Rust security team removed them and locked the account.

incidents.vector: Breach of the national road traffic agency's systems exposing records dating back to 2008.
incidents.impact: Personal information, payment receipts and license-plate details of 1.2 million Latvian citizens were stolen; CSDD leadership resigned following the hack.

incidents.victim: Global web servers (government, education, media, technology, gaming)
incidents.vector: UAT-10147 exploits known one-day flaws (Zimbra, Nacos, AjaxPro) and uses agentic AI to automate exploitation, then deploys BadIIS and the cross-platform SPECTRE implant with BYOVD EDR-killer and Linux rootkit capabilities.
incidents.impact: Financially motivated SEO-fraud and data-theft campaign hit Windows and Linux servers in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam, with a target list of roughly 170,000 URLs.

incidents.victim: Academics, aerospace/defense, governments and think tanks in Europe and the US
incidents.vector: Three suspected Russian clusters abuse legitimate authentication flows — app-password, OAuth and device-code phishing — impersonating the US State Department, embassies and forums like GLOBSEC.
incidents.impact: Persistent, adaptive social-engineering campaigns compromise personal and enterprise accounts of individuals of interest to Russia across Europe, Ukraine and the US.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure operators (Siemens S7 PLC owners)
incidents.vector: Threat actors use internet-scanning services and AI-generated Python scripts built on snap7 to access internet-exposed Siemens S7 PLCs, masquerading as legitimate OT monitoring tools.
incidents.impact: CISA, NSA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of active reconnaissance and read/write access to PLC memory and ladder logic, assessed as pre-positioning for future operational effects against critical infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Medusa ransomware-as-a-service affiliates gain access via phishing and rapid exploitation of CVEs (Fortra GoAnywhere, BeyondTrust, ScreenConnect, Fortinet EMS), often within 24 hours of disclosure.
incidents.impact: Updated FBI/CISA/HHS advisory reports Medusa has impacted over 500 victims using a double-extortion model that encrypts data and threatens to leak stolen files.

incidents.vector: PurpleDelta operators, likely based in China, use 22+ fabricated personas, AI-generated profile photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and real-time AI interview tools to secure remote technical jobs.
incidents.impact: Operators applied to over 1,100 companies and were likely employed at ten or more, funneling wages to the North Korean regime and posing an active insider-threat and data-theft risk.

incidents.vector: NERO R-ONE speed cameras — rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M devices — contain a backdoor granting shell and network access via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers, plus disabled Secure Boot and open live streams.
incidents.impact: Slovakia's NBU flagged 279 cameras bought under a €30M EU-funded project; the Interior Ministry paused deployment pending an independent audit.

incidents.vector: SynkLoader arrives via phishing from an attacker-registered Microsoft 365 tenant impersonating IT support, hosting a fake PowerShell tool on Azure storage; it bundles a Python multitool with fake Microsoft DLLs and a 'PhishLocker' fake lock screen to capture SSO passwords.
incidents.impact: New modular loader with system profiling, persistence, RAT and reverse-proxy modules; code and network-sizing behavior suggest it stages follow-on ransomware.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack affecting building-management systems at the hospital.
incidents.impact: The attack disabled access doors and heating, ventilation and air conditioning at Winnipeg's largest hospital, forcing added onsite security; clinical operations were reported unaffected.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack against municipal IT systems, prompting staff to disconnect affected agencies from the city network.
incidents.impact: The attack took down email, remote gateways and internet connectivity across Berlin's transport and urban development departments.

incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service floods claimed by the Iranian hacktivist '313 Team'.
incidents.impact: The DDoS attacks caused prolonged outages at BlueSky and GitHub over consecutive days.

incidents.victim: McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl, Gap and hotel chains
incidents.vector: An actor using the handle 'TheHatman' claims to have used compromised credentials, MFA-fatigue and password-spraying to access victims' Microsoft Entra (Azure) tenants; the specific intrusion vector is unverified.
incidents.impact: The actor is selling employee and enterprise data allegedly exfiltrated from roughly a dozen high-profile companies including McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl, Gap and the Intercontinental and Wyndham hotel chains.

incidents.vector: Data stolen from an external analytics service provider used by the exchange.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 250,000 customers of Israel's largest cryptocurrency exchange was stolen; the company notified customers over the weekend.

incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese hackers used publicly available AI tools, chaining Hermes and OpenClaw agents to automate reconnaissance, intrusion, lateral movement and data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Part of a wave hitting multiple Asian government networks, including a breach of Thailand's Ministry of Finance and Taiwanese government systems.

incidents.victim: Payment and shopping platform users (Shopify, PayPal, Apple, Klarna, banks)
incidents.vector: The 'JWR' phishing framework impersonates checkout and login pages across 44 phishing pages, streaming keystrokes and letting operators steer victim sessions live over an encrypted WebSocket; delivered via SMS lures spoofing toll, postal and courier services.
incidents.impact: Harvests full payment-card data, credentials, 2FA codes, SSNs and passport/ID images from victims in Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to CEVA's systems and began leaking customer data on the dark web.
incidents.impact: The breach at the French shipping and logistics firm disrupted freight delivery across large parts of Europe, affecting customers including Valve's Steam hardware business and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT professionals and system administrators
incidents.vector: A Sandworm sub-group (UAC-0145) scours job portals for Ukrainian IT professionals, contacts them via Telegram and arranges fake job interviews requiring download of Windows or Linux malware.
incidents.impact: CERT-UA reports the ongoing campaign, which began in May, likely aims to harvest credentials and pivot into government and company networks for intelligence collection.
